title: Flight Recorder: upgrade telemetry + LTS-aware rollout coordinator for Private deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Private (VPC/on-prem) customers require upgrade tooling that combines deterministic orchestration with rich upgrade telemetry. Current migration playbooks are manual, brittle across heterogeneous infra, and provide limited post-mortem visibility. Goal: deliver a coordinated upgrade controller for Private that (1) captures a comprehensive flight record for each upgrade, (2) drives LTS-aware rollout cohorts with programmable gates, and (3) executes orchestrated migrations (schema/state transforms) with dry-run and automated rollback capabilities. This ticket implements the control-plane pieces (controller + API + migration runner) and the telemetry flight-recorder used by Console and incident playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Flight Recorder captures pre-upgrade cluster snapshot, KV cache checkpoint hash, manifest of service versions, and per-node resource snapshot for each upgrade run
Coordinator supports LTS channel mappings and can resolve target version semantics (major.minor+lts tag) during plan creation
Canary cohorts can be defined by topology (AZ, node labels, tenant id) and stepped via programmable gates (latency, error-rate, custom metric) exposed as PromQL-like expressions
Migration runner supports a transactional dry-run mode (no writes) that produces an idempotent migration plan and a provenance report
Console UI shows a timeline of events from the Flight Recorder and exposes a one-click rollback to the last known-good snapshot
Automated rollback hooks invoke the state restore path and validate post-rollback health checks before marking rollback complete
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Preflight (week 0) - run compatibility matrix against sample manifests, validate operator permissions, create sample Flight Recorder entry via ‘upgradectl plan --dry-run’
Phase 1: Canary (week 1) - create 2 small cohorts (10% of nodes) with canary migration; monitor latency, error-rate, KV-cache hit-rate for 8 hours
Phase 2: Gradual (week 2) - expand cohorts to 50% if gates pass; run full migration hooks on a staging replica cluster
Phase 3: Sweep (week 3) - remaining nodes; final consistency checks and telemetry validation
Phase 4: Post-mortem (week 3+) - publish Flight Recorder artifacts, run data-diff checks, and update LTS compatibility matrix
migration_strategy: Prefer non-blocking schema changes using shadow-tables where possible; provide a built-in state-stitcher to migrate large KV blobs with chunked transforms
Each migration step declares a compensating action used by the rollback path
Migrations are ordered by data-dependency graph derived from a manifest; the runner runs independent steps in parallel where safe
Provide a ‘staged-apply’ mode where transforms are applied to a read-replica and validated before switching write traffic
telemetry_spec: Minimum recorded fields: timestamp, upgrade_id, cohort_id, node_id, pre_snapshot_sha, post_snapshot_sha, applied_migrations, error_codes, resource_metrics (cpu,memory,gpu), KV-cache diffs summary
Event model: checkpoints (pre, after-migration-step, post), signals (gate-pass, gate-fail), operator-actions (pause, resume, abort, rollback)
Retention: Flight Recorder entries kept for 90 days by default; export hooks for customers with longer retention requirements
Integrations: expose Flight Recorder artifacts to Console (timeline), to S3/MinIO for on-prem archival, and to our internal incident dashboard for regression alerts
decisions: Use a k8s controller for orchestrating Private clusters where kube is available; provide a fallback ‘upgradectl agent’ for air-gapped or non-k8s environments
Represent target versions via a canonical identifier (semver + LTS tag) to avoid ad-hoc version strings
Do not ship automated destructive schema rewrites by default; require opt-in with explicit operator acknowledgment
Telemetry payloads will be compressed ndjson blobs and signed with customer key when stored off-cluster
